comparisons.peer_topic: Segment accounting policies and performance measures
comparisons.peer_summary: The reportable operating segments use the same accounting policies as disclosed in Note 1, and the Chief Operating Decision Maker uses Income (loss) from continuing operations as the primary performance measure for evaluating and allocating resources to segments.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs (GS) and Citigroup (C) disclose the role of their Chief Operating Decision Maker (CODM) and the metrics used to evaluate segment performance. However, they differ in their primary performance measures: GS assesses performance based on a broader set of metrics including total net revenues, pre-tax earnings, and return on average common equity, whereas C identifies Income (loss) from continuing operations as the primary performance measure used by the CODM to evaluate results and allocate resources.

sentences.text: The firm's chief operating decision maker (CODM) is its president and chief operating officer.

The CODM makes operating decisions, assesses the performance of, and allocates resources to, the firm's operating segments principally based on the total net revenues of the segments, revenues net of provision for credit losses, total operating expenses, pre-tax earnings, net earnings applicable to common shareholders and the return on average common equity to assess the performance of the segments.
The accounting policies of these reportable operating segments are the same as those disclosed in Note 1.

The CODM uses Income (loss) from continuing operations as the performance measure, to evaluate the results of each reportable operating segment by comparing to and monitoring against budget and prior year results.

comparisons.peer_topic: Operating Committee Review of Segment Performance
comparisons.peer_summary: The Operating Committee reviews segment results, including net interest income, noninterest revenue, noninterest expense, provision for credit losses, and net income on a managed basis. These measures are used to evaluate segment performance and make key operating decisions, such as resource and capital allocations.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPMorgan Chase (JPM) disclose the metrics their respective decision-making bodies use to evaluate segment performance and allocate resources. GS states that its CODM assesses performance based on total net revenues, pre-tax earnings, and return on average common equity. Similarly, JPM’s Operating Committee reviews segment results including net interest income, noninterest revenue, noninterest expense, provision for credit losses, and net income on a managed basis to make key operating decisions and resource allocations.

sentences.text: The CODM makes operating decisions, assesses the performance of, and allocates resources to, the firm's operating segments principally based on the total net revenues of the segments, revenues net of provision for credit losses, total operating expenses, pre-tax earnings, net earnings applicable to common shareholders and the return on average common equity to assess the performance of the segments.
The CODM evaluates segment operating performance against the firm's targets and industry metrics and considers the current and future business and operating environment.
The Operating Committee reviews segment results including net interest income, noninterest revenue, noninterest expense, provision for credit losses and net income on a managed basis.
The Operating Committee uses these measures to evaluate segment performance and to make key operating decisions, including resource and capital allocations.

comparisons.peer_topic: Chief Operating Decision Maker and Segment Performance Evaluation
comparisons.peer_summary: The Firm's Chief Executive Officer serves as the CODM, evaluating segment performance and allocating resources based on business, strategic, and financial considerations including income before taxes, pre-tax margin, and return on average common equity.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and Morgan Stanley (MS) identify their senior executive as the CODM and specify financial metrics used to evaluate segment performance and allocate resources. GS identifies its president and COO as the CODM, using metrics like total net revenues, pre-tax earnings, and return on average common equity. MS identifies its CEO as the CODM, using financial considerations such as income before taxes, pre-tax margin, and return on average common equity. Both firms highlight 'return on average common equity' as a key metric in their performance assessment.
